title: Telemetry-driven rollforward plan for batch & cache regressions
creator: Priya Rao
description: Goal: design and implement a telemetry-driven automatic remediation system that prefers automated rollforward fixes for config-induced regressions affecting batching and KV cache behavior, with bounded fallback to full rollback. Background: recent config changes (batching window, cache TTL multipliers, kernel scheduling hints) caused transient cost spikes and tail-latency regressions. Pure auto-rollback creates thrash and lost optimizer state; pure rollforward risks hiding systemic failures. This ticket proposes a hybrid flow: detect anomalies via streaming telemetry, quarantine affected KV-cache prefixes, attempt safe rollforward patches (tunable), rehydrate caches from snapshot or partial replay, and if restoration fails against SLOs revert to a controlled rollback. The implementation will include trigger thresholds, hysteresis, canary-stage rollforward, state reconciliation reconciler, and operator-visible runbook UI. Focus areas: 1) telemetry signal definitions (cost per token, p95/p99 latency deltas, KV cache hit-rate, prefix miss storms); 2) quarantine mechanism for stale/poisoned KV prefixes with fast-evict and replay; 3) rollforward patch types (config tweak reversal, incremental throttle, batching window shrink, cache TTL adjustments); 4) rollback fallback with preserved snapshots and incremental replays to reduce cold-start cost; 5) safety guardrails (max rollforward attempts, time budget, automated pauses for infra alerts); 6) audit trail and postmortem links for any automatic action. This ticket covers design, prototype automation, integration tests using workload simulator, and a limited production canary on Dedicated pools.

acceptance_criteria: Automated detector emits anomaly event when configured thresholds crossed (cost/token > baseline*1.18 OR p99 latency increase > baseline + 120ms) for traffic > 30s
Quarantine API can evict and isolate affected KV-cache prefixes and prevent stale-key reuse without full cache flush
Rollforward action types (batching-window-shrink, cache-ttl-downscale, throttle-increase) can be applied via the config apply path and rolled back programmatically
A controlled canary runs: 5% traffic for 10 minutes, metrics validate improvement rule (p99 down or cost down) before progressive rollout
If rollforward fails safety checks within 15 minutes or degrades customer-facing SLOs by >10%, system performs rollback using snapshot-compatible restore path and emits an audit event
Integration test harness reproduces two failure modes and validates that the system chooses rollback when kernel-level faults are detected
decision_log: Chosen approach: prefer rollforward patches that are local and reversible to avoid full service churn. Rollforward attempts limited to 3 tries per incident with exponential backoff and operator notification. Quarantine rather than full flush to preserve warm cache state for unaffected prefixes. Rollback remains the ultimate fallback; to reduce cost impact we will support incremental replay from encrypted snapshots. Rationale: reduces user-visible cold-starts and unit cost while containing regression surface.
